content.comment_body: I'm attempting to establish communication between my PC and a [product_name], but it's not working. I've tried multiple PCs and confirmed that the network cards are functioning correctly—when connected to a router, internet access is fine. This [product_name] lacks a display, but I have a screen connected that allows me to view information. My current network configuration is: [product_name] IP 192.168.0.1, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 192.168.0.0; TDE screen IP 192.168.0.2, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 192.168.0.0. When connecting only the PC and [product_name], sometimes the software prompts me to change the subnet mask. When the network cable is just connected to the PC, the system detects a network failure. Is there something else I should try?
What are the IP addresses of your PC and router?
Router IP details: 192.168.1.152, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 192.168.1.1. The exact PC IP is not clear. I connect the [product_name] after unplugging the router.
For the PC, running 'ipconfig' shows: IP auto configuration 169.254.243.246, subnet mask 255.255.0.0, and no gateway.

You can leave the router on when trying to connect to the [product_name]. All devices should have IP addresses in the same range, using the format 192.168.1.x. Since your router is at 192.168.1.1 and your PC is at 192.168.1.152, assign the [product_name] IP 192.168.1.10, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 192.168.1.1, and for the TDE screen, IP 192.168.1.11, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 192.168.1.1.

Sorry for overlapping responses. When you connect the [product_name] directly to the PC (no router), and the PC IP auto-assigns: IP 169.254.243.246, subnet mask 255.255.0.0. Set the [product_name] to: IP 169.254.243.1, subnet mask 255.255.0.0, no gateway. Assign the TDE: IP 169.254.243.2, subnet mask 255.255.0.0, no gateway.
I'm unable to change the IP of the [product_name]; this device has a display.

To change IP settings, create a simple program (e.g., input to output). Under File > Properties > Offline Settings > General, you can set the new IP address and subnet mask. Transfer this program to the [product_name]. During connection setup, a window will appear; enter the current device IP. After pressing OK to transfer, you'll be prompted to overwrite the IP—confirm it, and the new IP address will be assigned.
I have to stop testing for now but will try again tomorrow. Thanks!

Here's another approach you can try: 1) Disconnect the PC from all Ethernet except the one linked to [product_name], including disabling WLAN/WiFi. 2) Start a fresh program in [product_name] configuration software—just link an input to an output. 3) Hit the download button. 4) In the interface dialog, don't enter any IP address; just click 'Scan' (blue cycle icon). 5) Accept any pop-up messages; the software will auto-configure your PC's Ethernet setup, which could take around a minute. 6) Once done, you should see the connected [product_name] IP in the interface dialog. 7) Use the address book feature to store the [product_name] IP, and select it for future use, speeding up connections. Be aware: if multiple Ethernet interfaces are active, the software may not detect [product_name]. It's better to configure the correct interface manually if your network demands more than one. Hope this helps!

I think I managed to resolve communication between the notebook and the [product_name]. I uninstalled and reinstalled the network card driver, rebooted, created a network, and set a static IP in the TCP/IP protocol: IP 192.168.0.254, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, no gateway. This seems to have fixed the issue, and the connection is now reliable—hoping it remains so. Now, I just need to fix communication with the desktop PC. I have a router with four available ports but can't configure it. Connecting [product_name] to these ports results in no detection, and the same happens when the notebook is connected.
Just a quick check: when connecting the [product_name] directly to the PC (without a router), did you use an Ethernet crossover cable?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering challenges in configuring direct Ethernet connections between a PC and [product_name], particularly due to mismatched IP addresses and subnet masks. Changing the device’s IP address is not straightforward—especially for versions without a display—making network setup unintuitive for many. Solutions often require users to have intermediate understanding of both the product and networking principles, resulting in uncertainty and repeated troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a simple and clear process for PC-to-[product_name] network setup, aiming to configure network settings quickly to facilitate programming and diagnostics.
